primary_mechanisms.observation: Capacitive feedback converts sensor charge to output voltage; a parallel resistive path supplies DC/reset authority and fixes the low-frequency pole. Applied as a physical instrumentation analogy, not a copied microphone circuit or proof of capsule safety.
Driven guarding controls leakage/capacitance across external insulation. Guard tracking and noise remain finite. ADA4530-1 input-current performance is not assigned to OPA197.

Input current noise, feedback resistance and voltage-noise gain with sensor capacitance affect current-input noise. A BJT base-current path therefore needs pressure-referred noise evidence, even when DC converges.

Floating excitation and differential capacitance sensing are instrumentation precedents. The slow digital converter is not selected for the audio path. Carrier oscillator, demodulator, folded noise and power must be validated separately.
